newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE MULLS CIRCUIT BREAKERS, CLOSING FIX.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE MULLS CIRCUIT BREAKERS, CLOSING FIX.

text.p: The Brussels bourse is considering the introduction of circuit breakers, a fixing procedure at the close and a variable closing time in order to reduce the volatility of its Bel-20 share index.
"We are considering various measures to limit Bel-20 volatility, a decision will probably be taken in January," Brussels bourse deputy chairwoman Anne Vleminckx told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The planned measures are in response to occasional wild swings of the Bel-20 in the last minutes of trading.

In March the bourse started a study into possible price manipulation by index-linked mutual funds. As many of these funds' reference prices were based on the closing price of the index over a period of days (rather than an average price) funds had an interest in pushing up the index towards the close.
Vleminckx declined to say whether any manipulation had been discovered, but added that the bourse was not only looking at volatility at the close of trade, but during the whole session.
"The volatility and the high volumes sometimes seen at the close of trade have made us think about managing volatility throughout the day," she said.

Vleminckx said that a fixing procedure at the close would be the easiest to introduce, as the Brussels bourse's NTS trading already uses that feature in the pre-opening of the forward market and for all trading on the cash market.

During a fixing, brokers can enter their orders, while they get some information (like best bids and offers) about other brokers' orders. A computer then calculates the fixing price at which the highest volume of orders can be executed.
Vleminckx said that a fixing at the close could imply that the bourse would have to stay open about 15 minutes longer than its normal closing time of 1630 local (1530 GMT).
A closing fixing was used once in September when the bourse introduced new weightings for the Bel-20 index shares.
Vleminckx said a circuit breaker would be more difficult to introduce, as it involves reprogramming trading computers.
"Using a circuit breaker means halting trade in index futures and in the underlying shares, and necessitates a warning system for all market participants," she said.

On Wall Street, circuit breakers temporarily halt trading once the Dow Jones moves more than a certain number of points in a short space of time. Vleminckx said there was no agreement yet on Bel-20 circuit breaker trigger levels.
She said that the trigger level could be a percentage change compared to the opening price or a percentage change in a given time period during the trading session.
The Brussels bourse already has the possibility to temporarily halt trading in individual forward market stocks when they move more than five percent during the session.
She said it was not sure yet when the new measures would take force. She added that Belgian futures and options exchange Belfox would be working closely with the Brussels bourse on the issue.
